references.text: The Lord promised to bring Israel out of Egypt and to be their God, so that they would know that he is the Lord.
Moses and Aaron are named as those who led the children of Israel out of Egypt.
The Lord brought the children of Israel out of Egypt, which is the central event referred to.
The Lord confirms that Israel shall know that he is their God who brought them out of Egypt.
Israel shall know that the Lord is their God who brought them out of Egypt.
The Lord identifies himself as the one who brought Israel out of Egypt to be their God.
The Lord reminds Israel that he brought them out of Egypt to be their God.
The Passover meal was to be eaten in the evening, in remembrance of the exodus from Egypt.
Both verses use the departure from Egypt as the decisive theological proof of God's faithfulness and power.
Samuel confirms and applies Moses' claim that the Lord alone brought the people out as the basis for the nation's identity.
Creates a theological contrast between God's sovereignty (Ex 16) and Moses' role as leader (Ex 33) in the exodus.
Contrast between the correct claim of God's salvation (Ex 16) and the people's mistaken attribution of glory to Moses (Acts 7).
